answer: Each seat is bound to one legal parcel, a meadow on its own knoll, with a county assessor number two years on the tax roll. The seed picks a depth band and a thirty-metre offset in that parcel; within a day a certified sampler pulls five cores there, logs GPS and a photo, and a lab assays organic carbon by dry combustion, returning a batch ID. Parcels sharing an owner, a lease, or a sampler and lab batch fold into one vote and forfeit 75,000 POA each. Assays and farm calls run about $565 per seat per epoch before any lease, and nobody fakes a plume of dust off an auger from a server.
